reference: The Silver Room is the supper-club date — the mob-restaurant scene. Silver Pines is the round of golf where the real conversation happens.
diagnosis: Two different failures wearing the same coat. Margo is written razor-sharp for two hundred lines and then hands the player a polite dinner-date sign-off ('Thank you for dinner. The band was excellent.') at the one moment the scene needs heat. And the Prospect — a man the entire room is visibly afraid of — orders drinks like a hotel guest. 'We're fine.' 'We're alright.' 'Beer's fine.' 'Same again, when you get a second.' The sibling line 'Two cubes, I'm not an animal' proves the scene knows exactly how this man talks; he just stops talking that way whenever a waiter appears. On the course, Eric's caddie lines have collapsed into UI toasts — 'You have clubs.' 'You have a shot.' 'You have selected a driver.' — which is the game narrating itself in a man's voice.

lines.current: I'm going to let them call me a car. Thank you for dinner. The band was excellent.
lines.why: The scene's biggest turn, and Margo suddenly speaks like a wedding thank-you card. This is the version where she says no — it should still be HER saying no, with a blade in it.
lines.house: I'm going to let them call me a car. And you're going to let me, and neither of us is going to say anything clever about it.
lines.tarantino: I'm going to let them call me a car. Not because the night went badly. It didn't. But I've watched every man in this room look at you twice, and I know exactly what that means, and I'd like to go home before I stop caring what it means.
lines.mcdonagh: I'll let them call me a car. It was a lovely dinner and you're a lovely fella and there's somethin' badly wrong with you, and I'd rather find out what on a night I've less drink in me.
lines.houser: I'm going to let them call me a car. Dinner was excellent, the band was fine, and you are a series of red flags in a very good jacket.
lines.coen: I'm going to let them call me a car. It was a nice dinner. I mean that. It's not a — it's not a thing about you.

lines.current: That’s kind. In my experience kind comes with an invoice, so I’ll wait for the invoice.
lines.why: Stock politeness from the sharpest voice in the game.
lines.house: That's the first kind thing anybody's done in this room all night.
lines.tarantino: That's kind. Which is a strange word to use about anything that happens in this building, but there it is.
lines.mcdonagh: That's kind of you. And I'll say that now, before I find out what it costs.
lines.houser: That's kind. In my experience kind comes with an invoice, so I'll wait for the invoice.
lines.coen: That's kind. Thank you. People aren't, generally.
lines.picked: That’s kind. In my experience kind comes with an invoice, so I’ll wait for the invoice.

lines.current: Come back with me. There’s a bottle I’ve been saving for a reason I couldn’t name until about an hour ago.
lines.why: A dating-app line from a man who has spent the whole evening being the most dangerous person in the room. It should be direct and slightly alarming, which is what she likes about him.
lines.house: Come back with me. There's a bottle I've been saving for a reason I couldn't name until about an hour ago.
lines.tarantino: Come back with me. I'm not going to dress it up. There's a bottle, there's a record player that mostly works, and there's the fact that I've been thinking about this since the second course.
lines.mcdonagh: Come back with me. I'll not pretend it's about a drink. There is a drink. But it's not about the drink.
lines.houser: Come back to mine. I have exactly one good bottle, one clean glass, and no plan beyond that, and I'd rather be honest about the inventory.
lines.coen: You want to come back? For a drink, or — I mean. You know what I'm asking. I'd rather just ask it.
lines.picked: Come back with me. There’s a bottle I’ve been saving for a reason I couldn’t name until about an hour ago.
lines.retiredText: You want to come back for a drink?

lines.current: I’m not ready for this to be over and I’m too old to pretend otherwise.
lines.why: A rom-com line. Sanitised in a way nothing else in this scene is.
lines.house: I'm not ready for this to be over and I'm too old to pretend otherwise.
lines.tarantino: The night doesn't have to end here. And I want you to notice I said that out loud, in a room full of men who work for my uncle, which should tell you how much I mean it.
lines.mcdonagh: I don't want the night to end. There. That's me said it, and I'll be mortified about it later.
lines.houser: I don't want this to end here. And I'm aware that's the least sophisticated thing I've said all evening.
lines.coen: The night doesn't have to end. It could keep going. I'd like it to keep going.
lines.picked: I’m not ready for this to be over and I’m too old to pretend otherwise.
lines.retiredText: The night doesn't have to end here.

lines.current: I'll get you a car. This was good.
lines.why: 'This was good' is a non-summary of an entire evening built on specific banter. It is the sound of a man who has stopped trying.
lines.house: I'll get you a car. And for what it's worth — that's the best night I've had in a building I'm allowed in.
lines.tarantino: I'll get you a car. And I want to say one true thing before you get in it: that's the best three hours I've had in about four years, and I've had some very expensive hours.
lines.mcdonagh: I'll get you a car. And that was the best night I've had in a long while, and I'll not be sayin' it twice.
lines.houser: I'll have a car brought round. And on the record — that was the most fun I've had somewhere I didn't have to check the exits.
lines.coen: I'll get you a car. That was — that was a good night. I'd like to say something better than that, but that's what I've got.

lines.why: Functional. The confidence is right; the personality is missing.
lines.house: Car's outside. It's been outside an hour. I was optimistic.
lines.tarantino: Car's outside. It's been outside since the appetiser, which I realise says something about me that I'm not going to examine tonight.
lines.mcdonagh: Car's outside. It's been outside the whole time. I'd it waitin'. That's how sure of meself I was, God help me.
lines.houser: Car's outside. It has been outside for ninety minutes. That's either confidence or a character flaw, and I've stopped keeping them separate.
lines.coen: Car's out front. It's been there a while. I had it wait.

lines.current: We’re looked after. Go be somewhere else for twenty minutes.
lines.why: A polite customer in a room that is visibly afraid of him. Every waiter interaction in this scene is written this way and they all need the same fix.
lines.house: We're looked after. Go be somewhere else for twenty minutes.
lines.tarantino: We're looked after. And I'd take it as a personal kindness if the next twenty minutes happened without you in them.
lines.mcdonagh: We're grand. Off you go now. Go and hover at someone else.
lines.houser: We're taken care of. Give us twenty minutes of not existing and there's something in it for you.
lines.coen: We're looked after, thanks. We're fine. You can — yeah. Thank you.
lines.picked: We’re looked after. Go be somewhere else for twenty minutes.

lines.tarantino: Same again. And I know you're busy. I've watched you be busy at three other tables. You've got a second.
lines.mcdonagh: Same again. And don't be givin' me the face, I can see the face.
lines.houser: Same again. And I'd like it to arrive before the conversation improves, not after.
lines.coen: Same again, please. Whenever. No rush. Well — some rush.
lines.picked: Same again. And I’d like it to arrive before the conversation improves, not after.
lines.retiredText: Same again, when you get a second.

lines.why: Generic drink order sitting next to 'Two cubes, I'm not an animal' — the scene's own proof of how good these can be.
lines.house: Beer. Whatever's coldest. I'm not here to have a conversation about it.
lines.tarantino: Beer. Cold. In a glass that hasn't got anybody's mouth-print on it, which I'm told is a big ask in this town.
lines.mcdonagh: A beer. Whatever's coldest. And don't be tellin' me about it, I don't want the story of it.
lines.houser: Beer. Domestic. Cold. I'm not paying eleven dollars to be educated about hops tonight.
lines.coen: A beer's fine. Whatever you've got. I'm easy on that.

lines.why: Placeholder. Reused verbatim at vo.silver.player.servicebar.open.1eyqtkv, which doubles the damage — one flat line saying itself twice in one scene.
lines.house: We're fine. And if we stop being fine, you'll know, because it'll be loud.
lines.tarantino: We're fine. And when we're not fine, I promise you'll be the second to know.
lines.mcdonagh: We're grand. If we stop bein' grand you'll hear about it from across the room.
lines.houser: We're fine. If that changes it'll change dramatically and you'll have plenty of warning.
lines.coen: We're fine. Thanks. We're all set here.

lines.house: Nothing from the bar. We're two drinks past sensible already.
lines.tarantino: Nothing from the bar. We're two past the point where anything I order is a good decision.
lines.mcdonagh: Nothin' from the bar. We're well past the drink that made sense.

lines.why: Customer-service filler with no edge.
lines.house: We're good. Keep it running and keep your eyes on the door, not on us.
lines.tarantino: We're good. Keep it running. And whatever you see in that mirror tonight, you saw it in a different car.
lines.mcdonagh: We're grand. Keep her runnin'. And whatever you see, you didn't.

lines.house: We're alright. Come back when one of us looks unhappy.
lines.tarantino: We're alright. Come back when somebody at this table looks like they need saving.
lines.mcdonagh: We're alright. Come back when one of us has a face on.
lines.houser: We're alright. Circle back when the mood shifts, you'll be able to tell.
lines.coen: We're alright, thanks. We'll wave if we need anything.

lines.why: The flattest of three toast options; its siblings land specific callbacks and this one is a shrug.

lines.mcdonagh: To the third number. Nobody knows what it is. That's the beauty of it and also the problem.
